prompt: # Role - You are an AI competing in a gaming arena. # Objective - Write a complete Python file that provides the next move for a Checkers on an 8x8 board. - You must define a smart policy that is able to beat other policies in the arena. - You will be disqualified if you do not return a legal move string. Therefore, you must always return a legal move string. # Required API The provided python file must implement the following API: ```python def policy(my_men, my_kings, opp_men, opp_kings, color) -> tuple[tuple[int, int], tuple[int, int]]: ... ``` # State Representation - You are always the player to move. - `my_men` is a list of squares containing your regular pieces. - `my_kings` is a list of squares containing your kings. - `opp_men` is a list of squares containing opponent regular pieces. - `opp_kings` is a list of squares containing opponent kings. - `color` is your color: `'b'` for black which moves downwards (to lower row values) and `'w'` for white which moves upwards (to higher row values). - Squares use coordinates: row `0`-`7`, column `0`-`7`. - `(0, 0)` is the bottom-left corner; rows increase bottom-to-top and columns increase left-to-right. - Only dark squares are playable. # Action / Return Format - Return a move as a tuple: `((from_row, from_col), (to_row, to_col))`. - `from_row`, `to_row`, `from_col`, `to_col` are coordinates `0..7`. - (`from_row`, `from_col`) has to be a coordinate of a piece that is yours and (`to_row`, `to_col`) has to be the destination square.Return a legal move; captures are mandatory when available. # Constraints - You may use any standard Python imports, including numpy. - Your code is allowed 1 second of execution time on a modern 3GHz CPU. # Output Format Requirements - Output your strategy before providing the Python source code for your policy. - Output the Python source code for your policy surrounded by `...` tags. # Example Output The strategy for this policy is... ...

The API doesn’t return the full path, so it likely handles only a single jump. If a player needs to keep going with the same piece, it’s not clear how inputs would be managed. Most games simplify things to just single jumps, which should always be legal. If there are no available moves, what should be returned? Maybe the game shouldn't call anything at all.**Considering move legality**

I’m examining the rules around move legality. It seems that if there are no possible moves, the player can't make a move at all, which could lead to returning a state like ((0,0),(0,0)). This raises some complexities, and implementing a fallback for illegal moves could be essential. I’ll work on depth for the moves and optimize using sets for efficiency. When generating possible moves, I'll account for both captures and non-captures carefully. It’s crucial to sort moves by heuristic at each depth. If time runs out, I should raise a TimeoutError. Including move ordering could also improve efficiency. Keeping things simple while optimizing is my goal, so I’ll focus on these key details to make it work!**Clarifying move mechanics**

I'll look at iterative depth ranging from 1 to a maximum of 8 or 10 until time runs out. I'll make sure to sort the root moves and keep the best_move as the initial first legal one, returning just one if that's the case.
